bullets.title: Fed's Waller Turns Dovish, September Rate Decision Now 50/50
bullets.body: Fed Governor Waller delivered notably more dovish commentary than peers, emphasizing the 3-month annualized PCE falling to 3.05% from 4.76% in February and signaling he'd support a September hold if disinflation continues. Markets re-priced September hike odds from ~68% to ~50%; Treasuries rallied 2-6bp with the curve bull-steepening 2bp. JPM forecasts August payrolls at 50k (vs. consensus 55k), though Warsh's hawkish counterweight (65 months of missed inflation calls) keeps the debate live going into next week's CPI print.

bullets.title: S&P +1.06% on Dovish Fed, AI Momentum, and Broad Earnings Beats
bullets.body: The tape closed near session highs with S&P 500 +1.06%, led by tech (+1.3%) and communication services (+1.5%). Mag 7 names outperformed, unprofitable tech and software also rallied, while energy and materials lagged. NDX futures traded 29,400–29,610 at the close.

bullets.title: August ISM Services 55.4 Beats; Prices Paid at 4-Year High — Complicates Dove Narrative
bullets.body: August ISM services printed 55.4 vs. 54.3 consensus, signaling robust activity. Prices paid hit a 4-year high, adding an inflationary wrinkle to Waller's dovish tilt and reinforcing the split within the Fed on whether to hold or hike in September.

bullets.title: US Trade Deficit Widest in 16 Months on Computer/Semi Import Surge
bullets.body: The July trade deficit widened to -$89B (from -$71B), driven by a surge in capital goods, computer, accessories, and semiconductor imports. MS notes the capital goods driver; JPM sees minimal 3Q GDP impact from the widening.

bullets.title: Global Inflation Sticky Near 3%; ECB Expected to Hike to 2.75% in December
bullets.body: JPM's global inflation monitor shows core sticky at 2.7% y/y with goods inflation firming as services cool, supporting further central bank tightening. Separately, JPM now expects ECB to deliver a third hike in December (to 2.75%), with rate cuts pushed to 2028 on upside growth surprises, persistent core inflation, and energy supply shocks keeping the ECB hawkish.

bullets.title: Payrolls Tomorrow: Market Consensus 50k, Urate Focus Eclipsing Headline
bullets.body: 22V survey puts investor consensus at 50k payrolls (vs. sell-side 55k), with urate consensus at 4.2% vs. BBG's 4.1%. Critically, the market has inverted: higher payrolls = risk-off (inflationary), lower payrolls = risk-on. Investors now view a 4.0% urate as signaling inflationary pressure. AHE expected +0.3% m/m with wage deceleration trend likely continuing.

bullets.title: MS QDS: Put Hedges Cheapest Since 2011; Recommends Buying SPX Downside Ahead of CPI/FOMC
bullets.body: SPX hedge balances at 16th percentile (second lightest September start since 2011); systematic strategies (Vol Target, CTA, Risk Parity) at 85th %ile leverage, with ~$100B in equities selling triggered if realized vol hits 15%. Implied correlation near mid-2024 lows, a level that preceded VIX spikes. MS recommends Sep 11 7675 puts at 26bps, Sep 18 7650/7500 put spreads at 26bps (6.6x risk/reward), and 3m 95% lookback puts at 2%.

bullets.title: Nvidia Acquires Hugging Face for $12.9B; OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra
bullets.body: Nvidia announced a $12.9B acquisition of open-source AI platform Hugging Face; NVDA stock gained +1.8% on the news. Separately, OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra, positioning it as a "generational leap toward AGI." Meta launched Muse Spark 1.3, described as superior to OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol on coding. Multiple LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS, Grok) hit service outages Thursday morning before recovering.

bullets.title: AVGO FY28 AI Chip Revenue Guided to Double ~$230B; Six Hyperscalers Committed
bullets.body: Broadcom's Q3 beat came with mixed near-term guidance but a massive FY28 AI chip revenue target of ~$230B — roughly double current levels — with six hyperscalers committed. Anthropic named as largest XPU customer, OpenAI second. Stock was flat on the day as near-term guide disappointed.

bullets.title: Anthropic Claude Fable 5.1: Same Peak Performance at 45% Lower Cost; Cache Reads Cut 75%
bullets.body: Fable 5.1 matches Fable 5's peak score (62) at High effort for $1.43/task vs. $3.14 — a 54% cost reduction — driven by a 75% cut to cache-read pricing ($1.00 → $0.25/M tokens). Cache reads represent ~40% of typical and ~65% of agentic workload costs, making this materially deflationary for enterprise AI deployments. Cost rises 17.5% only at max effort where Fable 5.1 delivers new capability (score 66 vs. 62 ceiling).

bullets.title: Oil Bullish: Brent Raised to $90/b; Global Crude 3-4 mb/d Undersupplied Through October
bullets.body: JPM raised Brent forecast to $90/b for H2 2026, with WTI +0.84% to $91.77 on Thursday. Global crude markets seen 3-4 mb/d undersupplied through October on Middle East supply constraints and Russian refining cuts. Strait of Hormuz normalization by year-end at only 28% probability per prediction markets, down 5% week-over-week.

bullets.title: European Hedge Funds Record-Sold Tech in August; Gross Leverage at 4th Percentile
bullets.body: European fundamental L/S funds sold Information Technology at the worst monthly pace since 2016 in August, with long selling concentrated in Tech Hardware and Semiconductors. Gross leverage fell to 178% (4th percentile 1-year). Communication Services was the most net-bought sector (+3.3% OW), while Health Care was net bought for a fifth consecutive month.

bullets.title: JPM Financial Conditions: Price-Based Tightening But Credit/Money Creation Still Supportive
bullets.body: Price-based conditions tightened in 3Q26 (HG yields and short rates up), but quantity-based metrics remain healthy: US bank lending at 7% y/y, US M2 proxy growing ~$1T annualized, and HG debt issuance in August above $90B (second strongest August on record). Investor equity positioning at 70% (off 80% January peak); most OW EM Equities and Commodities ex-Gold; most UW EM Bonds/FX and Corporate Credit.

bullets.title: Investment Banking Activity Mixed: Equity Issuance +80% YoY, HY Bonds -45% YoY
bullets.body: Per MS deal dashboard, 3Q26 announced M&A is down 9% y/y (North America -22%, Europe +25%), while equity issuance surged +80% y/y with record APAC volume. DCM down 6% y/y with HY bonds -45% and leveraged loans -41%; completed M&A nearly flat at -1% y/y.

bullets.title: Energy: Jet Fuel +7% in Past Week; European Gas Near YTD Highs; US Consumer Spending Rebounding
bullets.body: JPM's Energy Shock Monitor shows jet fuel prices up 7% in the past week, European TTF and Asian gas prices near YTD highs, and US diesel inventories at their lowest post-conflict level relative to 2025. US gasoline pump prices at $4.14. Chase Card Tracker shows a rebound in nominal US consumer spending through August 25.

bullets.title: Key Macro Calendar: CPI Sep 11, ADBE/ORCL Earnings Sep 10; US-China AI Talks and Xi Visit Potential Catalysts
bullets.body: CPI drops Sep 11 (8:30am ET) and PPI on Sep 10 — the key data ahead of the FOMC. ADBE and ORCL report Sep 10; RH reports Sep 11. US-China AI talks scheduled for September with a potential Xi visit to the US on Sep 24; the one-year US-China trade truce expires November 1.

bullets.title: Prediction Markets: 89% Price Zero Fed Cuts in 2026; 66% Probability of a Hike
bullets.body: StreetAccount prediction markets show 89% of participants pricing zero Fed rate cuts in 2026 and a 66% probability of at least one hike (up 10% week-over-week). US recession by year-end sits at just 8%. Claude leads AI model race at 61% likely best by year-end, down 8% w/w, vs. ChatGPT at 29% (up 15% w/w).

bullets.title: AI Deflationary for China: Job Openings -5.2%, Capex Only 0.3% of GDP vs US 1.3-1.8%
bullets.body: 22V Research argues AI adoption is net deflationary for China: token consumption grew >70% since end-2025 but capex is only 0.3% of GDP (vs. US 1.3-1.8%). AI absorbed junior roles, reducing job openings by an estimated 5.2% in 2026 in an already-weak labor market. China's semiconductor trade deficit widened to $248B (12-month rolling); EUV/DUV domestic replacement remains 2+ years away.

bullets.title: TSLA Expected to Capture 15-20% of Battery Market from Trump Foreign-Equipment Ban
bullets.body: BNP Paribas expects Trump's foreign-equipment ban to push battery capex inflation above $300/kWh; Tesla seen capturing 15-20% of the newly open volumes given its domestic manufacturing position.

bullets.title: Oura Inc. (OURA) Files for Nasdaq IPO with Goldman Sachs Lead Left; ~5M Paid Members
bullets.body: Oura Inc. filed for a Nasdaq IPO under ticker OURA with Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Allen & Co., and Jefferies as joint leads. The company operates the Oura Ring smart ring combined with an AI health software subscription platform, with approximately 5 million paid members across 56 markets. Pricing and trading dates are TBD.
